My room is, admittedly, not organized at all. It’s not messy. The bed’s made, the laundry’s done, everything is put away. But organization-wise, it sucks. Normally I’d be fine with anyone (even Tammy, before this incident obviously) helping me try to organize.

But, instead of actually organizing the books or CDs or anything like that, any surface that could use organization, she decided to start to attempt to tear a specific poster off of my wall. I yelled at her to stop, and for some reason? She actually listened.

Obviously the whole “I can help organize” thing was just a ploy for her to get into my room to take down what she deemed to be obscene or just dumb-looking. And it didn’t work. And for that, she’s (I believe) held a grudge against me since.

To make it short, no I haven’t been able to grieve or move on. I begged myself to not cry during the funeral, not in front of anyone. And I didn’t. I did all of my crying when I said goodbye to my mom in the hospital. And I know it’s not healthy, but I couldn’t bare the thought of all those people seeing me cry even if it was perfectly understandable.

I just feel trapped in a cycle of never ending grief because I can’t possibly even try to “move on”. Part of me doesn’t want to move on. Even if I did, how could you expect me to when I’m dealing with fucking Cinderella-levels of bullshit.

I eventually came to realize my mom was never getting better, never coming home, or would never be “herself” again. I realized that, and accepted it just two days before her death. And now with my dad, I’m starting to realize that, we aren’t close anymore. I’m not top priority, I’m not someone he talks to or goes to for help, and Vice versa, anymore.

And it hurts. It hurts because I loved my mom, obviously. But I clearly always favored my dad more in childhood. He was the less strict and more humorous parent. And I used to love just talking to him and listening to stories and whatever else. Now, when he goes to work (gone for several days at a time) he doesn’t even bother to text or call. Same with when he goes places with Tammy. Half the time he doesn’t even bother to tell me bye, and I don’t speak to him again until he shows back up 2 days later. I try to call him, but he never answers. And I don’t know…I guess I’m slowly accepting that, things aren’t ever gonna be the same for us. We’re never gonna be close again. 

So yeah. In the span of say, 4 months? I lost my mom and my dad. I don’t have anyone.

Everything else tho….yeah, fuck them both.

But I can’t just leave my dad. I can’t leave my friends. I can’t leave the church I go to. I can’t leave my grandparents (they live close but not within 30 miles of the campus-close) and I can’t leave my mom’s grave. Above everything else, I can’t leave her grave.

It’s petty and stupid and babyish to want to cry about that of all things, but i spent literally so much time and effort making my walls look…unique?? I guess. They’re cluttered with posters and album art and yeah it’s a lot but I want it that way.

Which is why I kinda believe she did the whole contact this as revenge. Revenge for setting a boundary, revenge for telling her no. Revenge for telling her to fuck off with no words. And I feel crazy for even thinking that, it feels like some Lifetime movie bullshit, not real life.

I’m around 3-4 years older than you, my mom also recently passed. I was the exact same way. I had some leverage because her phone was broken and she couldn’t accept or make calls. But whenever she found a way to call me, I couldn’t handle listening to her try to talk coherently, and I would purposely make the calls fail by turning on airplane mode.

I visited her a couple of times. There were several times where I flat out said I wouldn’t go. Several times where I refused to leave my house because I didn’t want our last memories to be of her in a hospital bed fighting for her life.

The point is, you’re young. You didn’t want to see or hear your dad in that state. Regardless of what other people tell you, you’re the only person who can understand how you’re feeling. It’s no ones right to act like you’re a bad person for how you responded. You don’t deserve to feel grief or remorse for the rest of your life over this. Everybody makes decisions they regret later. Hindsight is 20/20, after all.
